questions.explain: Organizations running a custom analyzer report 18–35% reductions in monthly database spend within 90 days — roughly $40,000–$120,000/year for a mid-sized org with 20–50 instances. The analyzer itself runs as a Lambda/cron/Cloud Run job costing under $15/month.
options: Custom analyzers cut spend 18–35% in 90 days (~$40k–$120k/yr for 20–50 instances) while costing under $15/month to run
Building is more expensive than it saves
questions.q: What results do custom database cost analyzers deliver?

questions.explain: Five components: (1) data collection layer — billing APIs + CloudWatch/monitor + Performance Insights/Query Store on a schedule; (2) metrics correlation layer — joins billing line items with CPU/memory/IOPS/connections; (3) rules engine — idle, right-sizing, storage, RI gaps, connection pools; (4) recommendations database — persists findings with status and savings estimates (the audit trail for Finance); (5) reporting layer — weekly email, Slack alerts, dashboard.
options: Data collection → metrics correlation → rules engine → recommendations database → reporting layer — persisted findings with savings estimates form the audit trail
questions.q: What are the five components of a database cost analyzer?

questions.explain: Finding types with typical savings: idle instance (avg CPU <5% over 14d, max <20%, conns <2) → 100%; oversized (avg <20%, max <40%, 30%+ memory headroom) → 40% (r6i.2xlarge $1,040 → xlarge $520); gp2→gp3 → 30.4% (1TB = $35.84/mo); Multi-AZ on non-prod → 50% ($2,080 → $1,040); missing RI, io1 candidates, stopped instances also covered. These four core rules surface 60–70% of total available savings.
options: All rules save the same amount

questions.q: What are the core rules engine findings and their typical savings?

questions.explain: The recommendations DB records cloud provider, resource ID, finding type, estimated monthly savings, confidence (high/medium/low), detection timestamp, and resolution status (open/actioned/dismissed) — the audit trail that justifies the analyzer to Finance and leadership. The v_open_savings_summary view totals open savings by provider and finding type for reporting.
options: Persist provider, resource, finding type, savings estimate, confidence, timestamps, and resolution status — the audit trail Finance needs; summarize open findings in a view
questions.q: What does the recommendations database record, and why?

questions.explain: Database-internal stats show what consumes the resources billing data charges for: Query Store / dm_exec_query_stats give per-query CPU and physical reads (each physical read is an 8KB storage page driving IOPS). Combined with billing: 'this $2,400/month instance is 60% consumed by three queries running 50,000 times/day — optimizing them could halve the instance cost' — the framing that gets engineering attention.
options: Query Store data shows what consumes the billed resources — per-query CPU and physical reads let you frame findings as 'three queries consume 60% of this $2,400/mo instance'
